summary: Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served at Hanazono University as a professor from circa 1987 to 2023, and became professor emeritus (名誉教授) there circa 2023.
Jeff Watt works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, mentored by Taitetsu Unno (attested 2009) and postdoctoral mentor Myosei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his BA at the University of Notre Dame and an MA and PhD at the University of Chicago, becoming Associate Professor at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor of religious studies at California State University, Long Beach (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Missouri State University and a PhD from UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, later serving as an assistant professor at Marshall University in 2002.
Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), advised by Sanghasen Singh and supervised by Collett Cox.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1972, he served as Associate Professor and Center Director at the University of Virginia from 1973 to 2005.

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago and was appointed the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University in 2002.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Komazawa University and Leiden University and held posts at McMaster University, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Cornell, Johns Hopkins, and Boston University (from circa 1983 as University Professor and Professor of French Literature), along with visiting professorships at several institutions.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and served as Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley from 1981 to 1992.
Jeffrey Newmark works in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University and the University of British Columbia, and held an academic post at the University of Winnipeg.
Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from UC Santa Barbara. He held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2003) and Berry College.

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).
Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1976 and served as a professor there from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, UT Knoxville, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later serving as an instructor and teaching associate at UCLA and a lecturer at UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, supervised by Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, with Geshe Lhundup Sopa as MA supervisor.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jenny Hung specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She earned PhDs from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Lingnan University, and serves as Assistant Professor of Humanities at HKUST.
